LESSON: WRITING 7.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING- DIALOGUE

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 7
Topic 7.3: Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue, part of Strand 7 in Grade 4 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: Why are interjections important?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. highlight the steps of writing a simple dialogue,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate the need of creative writing.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. highlight the steps of writing a simple dialogue,

   Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write a simple dialogue on the theme using interjections,

   Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate the need of creative writing.

   Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the steps of writing a simple dialogue,

2. list interjections used in their community on flashcards,

3. work with peers to write a simple dialogue on the theme using the interjections and share with peers,

4. team up to role play the dialogue while using interjections creatively,

5. collaboratively compose a simple singing game with interjections.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the steps of writing a simple dialogue,
2. list interjections used in their community on flashcards,
3. work with peers to write a simple dialogue on the theme using the interjections and share with peers,
4. team up to role play the dialogue while using interjections creatively,
5. collaboratively compose a simple singing game with interjections.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 7.3.1 Creative writing- Dialogue together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creative thinking and imagination: This is enhanced as the learner exchanges new ideas that inspire creativity when

composing a simple singing game with interjections.

• Communication and Collaboration: This is promoted as the learner engages actively with peers to role-play a dialogue while

using interjections.

42

Values:
• Unity: This is enhanced as the learner cooperates with peers to write a simple dialogue on the theme.

• Respect: This is shown as the learner ensures positive regard for others when role-playing the dialogue.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer pressure: This is addressed as the learner creatively writes a simple dialogue on leisure activities to promote values.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of dialogue to their learning of similar concepts in Kiswahili and English.
